narrative_purpose: The cover that captures the chapter at a glance: the hunt itself, a pack closing on a single prey animal in the dark, so the reader feels the predator-prey drama the chapter turns into mathematics.
subject: A tense hunting scene: a single small six-limbed deer-like browser stands frozen at the centre-right, head up and alert, a bright fan of skin flared open on its skull. Around it, low to the ground, three sleek black six-limbed pack-hunters fan out in a wide half-circle, bodies stretched in a stalking crouch, closing in from the left. Faint bioluminescent markings trace all four animals. The prey is the bright focal point; the hunters are darker shapes emerging from the gloom.
scene: A dim bioluminescent forest floor at night, glowing undergrowth and a few tall trunks receding into haze, drifting spores in the air.
camera: Naturalist low three-quarter view at the animals' eye level, the half-circle of hunters leading the eye toward the prey.
light: Brightest light from glowing flora low in the scene, rim-lighting the prey's flank and flared fan in cyan; the hunters' eyes catch faint glints.
palette: Cool teal-indigo dominant, the hunters in deep shadow, the prey lifted by cyan rim light, a scarce warm magenta glint in the predators' eyes.
style: Hand-painted naturalist field plate of real alien animals, textured and observed, not a film still.
detail_level: High on the four animals and the flared fan; soft and hazy on the forest behind.
composition: A reading half-circle of dark hunters on the left curving toward a single lit prey on the right, deep hazy depth, dark negative space above.
consistency_notes: The pack-hunters are the viperwolf archetype (sleek, black, six-limbed) and the prey is the hexapede archetype (small, six-legged, cranial display fan); both must read consistently across this chapter's figures.
